about_bio1: My name is Jeffery Asare. I am a photographer based in Accra, Ghana, working professionally with a full kit and personally with nothing more than an iPhone and a quiet obsession with the way light behaves when no one is paying attention to it.
about_bio2: I do not shoot with intention the way most photographers describe it: with mood boards and pre-visualised frames. I shoot because something stops me. A face. A shadow. The way a wall holds colour at the end of the day.
about_bio3: My work lives at the intersection of the ordinary and the overlooked. I am drawn to portraits that hold something back, to compositions that ask more than they answer, and to the kind of beauty that does not announce itself. I shoot on iPhone. I edit in Lightroom Mobile. I am not interested in what the camera cannot do, only in what I have not yet figured out how to see.
about_bio4: I want my photographs to slow people down, not to inspire in the broad, motivational sense, but to create a moment of pause. A second look. The feeling that something familiar has just revealed itself as strange, or something strange as deeply familiar.
about_bio5: My practice is built around the smartphone as a serious creative tool. I work with available light, ordinary scenes, and the kind of access that only comes from not carrying equipment. What I am after is not the extraordinary moment. It is the extraordinary quality hidden inside the everyday one.
about_loc_p1: Ghana does not ask to be photographed. It simply exists, loud and textured and indifferent to the lens, generous light in the morning, sharp by noon, forgiving by evening. I do not travel to exotic locations looking for striking images. The ordinary streets here contain more than I have managed to photograph in years of trying, and that is enough for a lifetime.
about_phil_p1: Most people walk past things. I am interested in the half-second before that, the moment something registers but has not yet been named. I use a phone because it closes the gap between noticing and capturing: no setup, no signal to the subject that something is being recorded, just attention. I edit the same way, intentional, entirely on the phone, finishing the sentence the moment started rather than manipulating it into something else.
about_street_p1: Much of my street and documentary work happens without asking first. A market stall, a corner, a face caught mid-thought: the moment exists because no one was told to hold still for it. I photograph with care, I don't chase people into situations that could embarrass or endanger them, and a photograph earns its place here because it holds something true on its own, never because of who happens to be in the frame.
about_street_p2: If you recognise yourself in one of these photographs and want to talk about it, whether that's a question or a concern, write to me at hello@jefferyasare.com. I take that seriously.
